subject: MedicaTeq production 429s and latency spikes — suspected rate/burst policy misconfiguration

On Wed, May 23, 2028 at 09:12 Alicia Ramos <aramos@medicateq.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sharp increase in 429s and end-to-end latency ...

Quick update from runtime: we've pulled the token-bucket and burst-policy traces for MedicaTeq's tenant for the 08:30–09:30 PT window. Preliminary root cause looks like a misapplied burst-window parameter during a policy rollout this morning. Specifically:

- policy_id RB-guard-723 was deployed with burst_window_ms=100 instead of the intended 1000 (decimal place error in a config template).
- The smaller window causes the runtime to exhaust burst credits far faster for bursty request patterns typical of MedicaTeq's checkout path. That results in immediate hard 429s from our guard and higher queuing latency behind the pacing layer.
- We see the token refill rate unchanged; this is a window sizing/regeneration cadence error — not model performance.

Attached: redis_qps_dump.log (short sample of token counter drops) and burst_policy_snapshot.txt (the active policy payload).

Mitigation options we can apply within minutes:
1) Temporarily increase tenant burst credits (adds headroom for ~30–60 minutes) — low-risk, immediate.
2) Re-deploy corrected policy with burst_window_ms=1000 (requires a quick config rollout and validation).
3) Revert today's policy rollout (if you prefer rollback-first).

I recommend option 1 + 2 (apply headroom, then deploy corrected policy). I'm ready to run the commands once Mina/Marissa confirm. I'll also push a short guard to prevent future decimal/shim-template misparses.

Grace

Attachment stubs:
- redis_qps_dump.log (log)
- burst_policy_snapshot.txt (policy payload)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <aramos@medicateq.com>

Subject: Re: Urgent: Production 429s + latency spikes

Alicia — thanks Grace, that explanation matches what MedicaTeq saw on our side. We're going to: 1) apply a temporary +200% burst credit lift for MedicaTeq, 2) deploy corrected policy with burst_window_ms set to 1000, and 3) monitor for the next 90 minutes.

Planned timeline:
- 10:10 PT: apply temporary credit lift (immediate effect).
- 10:18 PT: rollout corrected policy and validation on canary shard, then global if green.
- 10:45 PT: update customer with status and observed metrics.

We've also prepared a short runbook for this remediation (attached) and a postmortem template we'll share after stabilization. If you'd like, we'll schedule a 30-min postmortem with your SREs tomorrow.

Mina

Attachment: remediation_runbook.md (runbook stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T18:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-stabilization brief: MedicaTeq burst policy misconfig & customer impact

Jonas — brief summary and asks for exec awareness:

Summary:
- Impact window: 2028-05-23 08:50–10:45 PT.
- Customer: MedicaTeq (checkout flow). Observed: transient 429 spike (peak ~6%) and p95 latency increase to ~1.8s.
- Root cause: policy rollout introduced burst_window_ms=100 (should have been 1000) due to a templating decimal placement error. This reduced effective burst headroom for tenant traffic.
- Remediation performed: temporary +200% burst credits applied (10:10 PT), corrected policy rolled to canary + global (10:18–10:30 PT), monitoring and validation until 10:45 PT. Metrics returned to baseline after rollout.

Customer impact and commercial ask:
- MedicaTeq experienced failed checkouts during the window. They're requesting a goodwill credit for the affected window and a joint postmortem.
- Recommend offering a targeted credit (one day of served tokens at no charge) and committing to a joint postmortem + technical action items: improved templating validation, preflight policy dry-run, and a canary gating check for burst parameter anomalies.

Immediate asks for leadership:
1) Approve the proposed credit (one day token equivalent) for MedicaTeq.
2) Back a short initiative to add a templating validation step + automated policy preflight over the next 2 sprints.

I'll include the remediation commands and logs in the internal incident folder; attaching policy_change_cmds.txt for reference.

--
Marissa
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
